# Resource: stripe_plan

A legacy recurring price. Prefer `stripe_price` for new work. `terraform destroy` deletes the plan, which stops new subscriptions to it and leaves existing ones in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_product" "gold" {
  name = "Gold plan"
}

resource "stripe_plan" "monthly" {
  product  = stripe_product.gold.id
  currency = "usd"
  interval = "month"
  amount   = 2000
  nickname = "Monthly"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `currency` - (Required) Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies). Changing it replaces the resource.
* `interval` - (Required) Specifies billing frequency. Either `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`. Possible values: `day`, `month`, `week`, `year`. Changing it replaces the resource.

The following arguments are optional:

* `active` - (Optional) Whether the plan is currently available for new subscriptions. Defaults to `true`. Default (Stripe): `true`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `amount` - (Optional) A positive integer in cents (or local equivalent) (or 0 for a free plan) representing how much to charge on a recurring basis. Changing it replaces the resource. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `amount_decimal` - (Optional) Same as `amount`, but accepts a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places. Only one of `amount` and `amount_decimal` can be set. Changing it replaces the resource. Default (Stripe): the `amount` sent, as a decimal string (`1500` on a US account). Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `billing_scheme` - (Optional) Describes how to compute the price per period. Either `per_unit` or `tiered`. `per_unit` indicates that the fixed amount (specified in `amount`) will be charged per unit in `quantity` (for plans with `usage_type=licensed`), or per unit of total usage (for plans with `usage_type=metered`). `tiered` indicates that the unit pricing will be computed using a tiering strategy as defined using the `tiers` and `tiers_mode` attributes. Possible values: `per_unit`, `tiered`. Changing it replaces the resource. Default (Stripe): `per_unit`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `id` - (Optional) An identifier randomly generated by Stripe. Used to identify this plan when subscribing a customer. You can optionally override this ID, but the ID must be unique across all plans in your Stripe account. You can use the same plan ID in live mode and in your sandboxes. Changing it replaces the resource. Default (Stripe): generated by Stripe: a create that does not send it gets the new object's own ID. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `interval_count` - (Optional) The number of intervals between subscription billings. For example, `interval=month` and `interval_count=3` bills every 3 months. Maximum of three years interval allowed (3 years, 36 months, or 156 weeks). Changing it replaces the resource. Default (Stripe): `1`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`. Default (Stripe): `{}`.
* `meter` - (Optional) The meter tracking the usage of a metered price Changing it replaces the resource. Default: none.
* `nickname` - (Optional) A brief description of the plan, hidden from customers. Default: none.
* `product` - (Optional) The ID of the product whose pricing the created plan will represent. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `product_data` - (Optional) The product whose pricing the created plan will represent. This can either be the ID of an existing product, or a dictionary containing fields used to create a [service product](https://docs.stripe.com/api#product_object-type). Changing it replaces the resource. See [`product_data`](#product_data) below.
* `tiers` - (Optional) Each element represents a pricing tier. This parameter requires `billing_scheme` to be set to `tiered`. See also the documentation for `billing_scheme`. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`tiers`](#tiers) below.
* `tiers_mode` - (Optional) Defines if the tiering price should be `graduated` or `volume` based. In `volume`-based tiering, the maximum quantity within a period determines the per unit price, in `graduated` tiering pricing can successively change as the quantity grows. Possible values: `graduated`, `volume`. Changing it replaces the resource. Default: none.
* `transform_usage` - (Optional) Apply a transformation to the reported usage or set quantity before computing the billed price. Cannot be combined with `tiers`. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`transform_usage`](#transform_usage) below.
* `trial_period_days` - (Optional) Default number of trial days when subscribing a customer to this plan using [`trial_from_plan=true`](https://docs.stripe.com/api#create_subscription-trial_from_plan). Default: none.
* `usage_type` - (Optional) Configures how the quantity per period should be determined. Can be either `metered` or `licensed`. `licensed` automatically bills the `quantity` set when adding it to a subscription. `metered` aggregates the total usage based on usage records. Defaults to `licensed`. Possible values: `licensed`, `metered`. Changing it replaces the resource. Default (Stripe): `licensed`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="product_data"></a>
### `product_data`

The `product_data` attribute supports:

* `active` - (Optional)
* `id` - (Optional)
* `metadata` - (Optional)
* `name` - (Required)
* `statement_descriptor` - (Optional)
* `tax_code` - (Optional)
* `tax_details` - (Optional) See [`product_data.tax_details`](#product_data.tax_details) below.
* `unit_label` - (Optional)

<a id="product_data.tax_details"></a>
### `product_data.tax_details`

The `product_data.tax_details` attribute supports:

* `performance_location` - (Optional)
* `tax_code` - (Optional)

<a id="tiers"></a>
### `tiers`

The `tiers` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `flat_amount` - (Optional) Price for the entire tier. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `flat_amount_decimal` - (Optional) Same as `flat_amount`, but contains a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `unit_amount` - (Optional) Per unit price for units relevant to the tier. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `unit_amount_decimal` - (Optional) Same as `unit_amount`, but contains a decimal value with at most 12 decimal places. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `up_to` - (Required) Up to and including to this quantity will be contained in the tier.

<a id="transform_usage"></a>
### `transform_usage`

The `transform_usage` attribute supports:

* `divide_by` - (Required) Divide usage by this number.
* `round` - (Required) After division, either round the result `up` or `down`. Possible values: `down`, `up`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - The Stripe ID of the object.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a plan using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_plan.monthly
  id = "gold_monthly"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_plan.monthly
  identity = {
    id = "gold_monthly"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the plan.

Using `terraform import`, import a plan using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_plan.monthly gold_monthly
```

~> Stripe does not return `product_data`, so an imported plan has it null: a configuration that sets it plans a replacement after the import.
